questions.question_text: In secondary research studies, which of the following items is the unit of recruitment?
questions.explanation:
Secondary research refers to research conducted using data from other researches. Here individual patients are not recruited, instead
eligible studies are 'recruited'.

questions.question_text:
An old age psychiatrist is interested in reviewing the literature on hyponatraemia related to SSRI use. He has wide clinical experience on this
topic and chooses some key review papers as starting point and collates the information known to him already to provide a summary of
evidence. Which research method is he following?
questions.explanation:
Narrative reviews are usually carried out by experts in the �eld of study and are more or less close to an expert's opinion supported by
research evidence. These reviews are generally broad without a narrow or speci�c clinical question and are subjective. They carry a higher
risk of being prone to bias than systematic reviews. Nevertheless narrative reviews can provide a good introduction to a topic, stimulate
interest and controversies and can even collate existing data for generating new hypotheses.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of narrative review but not systematic review?

options.text: Literature search based on expert's familiarity

correct_answer.text: Literature search based on expert's familiarity

questions.explanation:
Narrative review usually involves a patchy literature search. Literature is not searched methodically but rather in a random manner
according to one's familiarity and to suit one's �ow of argument. Because of the above, narrative reviews cannot be replicated (unless
repeated by the same author!!).

questions.explanation:
It is usually RCTs that undergo meta-analysis. If the primary studies included have poor quality, then even if sound methodological and
statistical procedures are followed the outcome may be meaningless. This is called GIGO principle of 'garbage in, garbage out'!!

questions.question_text: Which of the following factor is the least/not important in determining the quality of a meta-analysis?

options.text: Comparability of intervention among individual studies
Magnitude of outcome reported from individual studies

correct_answer.text: Magnitude of outcome reported from individual studies

questions.explanation:
While determining the quality of a meta-analysis, one can consider 1. The nature of the patient sample, 2. Outcomes studied, 3. Lengths of
follow-up and 4. Comparability (e.g. dosage) of treatment. Methodological factors include adequacy of sample randomisation, adequate
concealment and control of intervention, analysis with intention to treat principles, and having an objective, blinded, outcome assessment.
The magnitude of outcomes as such does not re�ect the quality of trials.

questions.question_text: In which of the following situations a random e�ects analysis is indicated in a meta-analysis?

When combining the outcomes from di�erent studies, one may use a �xed and/or random e�ects model. A �xed e�ects model assumes

questions.question_text:
A reviewer notes the following while undertaking a literature search to identify the e�ect of vitamin E on tardive dyskinesia. Many small
studies are published only when they show a positive result in favour of vitamin E. But larger studies are published with both directions of
results. If the reviewer constructs an inverted funnel plot which of the following will be seen?

options.text: The plot will be asymmetrical due to the absence of small negative studies.
The plot cannot be constructed due to the lack of negative small studies
The plot will be smaller in size due to the presence of small studies
The plot will be asymmetrical due to the presence of large studies in both directions of results

correct_answer.text: The plot will be asymmetrical due to the absence of small negative studies.

questions.explanation:
The most common method to detect publication bias is to investigate the presence of asymmetry in (inverted) funnel plots. A funnel plot
shows the relation between study e�ect size and its precision. Small studies are more likely to remain unpublished if their results are
nonsigni�cant or unfavourable, and larger studies get published regardless. This leads to funnel-plot asymmetry. Although visual inspection
of funnel plots is unreliable, statistical tests can be used to quantify the asymmetry.

correct_answer.text: Di�erence in outcome between intervention and control groups

questions.question_text:

Researchers withhold negative results from publication

correct_answer.text: Researchers withhold negative results from publication

questions.question_text: Meta-analyses that summarise data from multiple studies are needed because

options.text: Individual studies are susceptible to confounding
Individual studies often use higher threshold of p values
Individual studies often lack su�cient power for generalised conclusions
Individual studies are prone to measurement errors

correct_answer.text: Individual studies often lack su�cient power for generalised conclusions

questions.explanation:
Remember GIGO principle in secondary research: Garbage in - Garbage out! The quality of a systematic review or meta-analysis depends on
the quality of individual studies. Hence error or bias-prone individual studies cannot be replaced by a meta-analyses of those studies. But
pooled data in a secondary study such as meta-analysis has larger sample size to achieve better precision.
Gene Glass coined the term in 1976 and described it as the "analysis of analyses".
